newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury calls for large position reports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury calls for large position reports.

text.p: The Treasury Departgment announced on Monday that it was calling for large position reports from anyone holding $2.5 billion or more of 10-year Treasury notes that mature on Feb 15, 2007.
Treasury said the call was a test, rather than a reflection of concern about a possible "squeeze" on the notes in which one party owns a disproportionately large amount of the issue.
Treasury said that anyone holding $2.5 billion or more of the notes at the close of business June 6 must report it to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York by 1200 EDT/1600 GMT on Friday, June 13.
It gives Treasury the information it needs to measure whether anyone is taking a huge position in any security, which potentially would give that holder power to influence prices.
Deputy Assistant Treasury Secretary Roger Anderson said that about $12 billion of the 10-year notes of Feb 2007 were sold.
He said that when Treasury published its rules last year for large position reporting, it said it would choose a threshhold of $2 billion or more for requiring reports.
"We've said that we would run tests about once a year and this is it," Anderson said.
